text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Fears that Namibia will go ahead with plans to draw water from the Okavango river even if the environmental impact assessment is unfavourable have surfaced in the Botswanan media.
- Insurance companies Sanlam Namibia and Old Mutual have welcomed the draft Long-Term Insurance Bill, requiring them to "demutualise" and change their operating structures.

- The Transportation Commission is expected to announce on Tuesday whether Kalahari Express Airlines has been granted the scheduled air service licence for flights from Eros airport to Johannesburg and Cape Town.

- Execuitves within the fishing industry in Walvis Bay feel that the sector cannot survive a zero Total Allowable Catch for pilchards next year, and that the government should reconsider its position in the light of latest surveys.
- Mismanagement at the Government Garage was found by an internal investigation as early as March this year.
